subject.title: fix(irc): disconnect on oversized inbound lines

question: Should an oversized inbound IRC record permanently stop the current channel connection, or should the plugin discard/recover or reconnect with bounded backoff?
rationale: Source and proof establish the memory bug and the correctness of the byte check, but repository behavior does not define whether a remote framing violation should trade memory safety for a lasting channel outage or how non-default IRC line lengths are supported.

options.title: Close and recover explicitly
options.body: Retain the strict disconnect, propagate the terminal socket state into the channel lifecycle, and reconnect with bounded backoff or a circuit breaker plus focused TCP recovery proof.

options.title: Discard the oversized record
options.body: Bound memory while discarding bytes through the next delimiter, log the violation, and keep the connection alive with a test proving subsequent legal messages are processed.

options.title: Accept permanent disconnect
options.body: Land the current fail-closed behavior only with explicit IRC-owner acceptance that a protocol violation requires operator or gateway restart and that fixed 512-byte compatibility is intentional.

recommendation.title: Close and recover explicitly
recommendation.body: Retain the strict disconnect, propagate the terminal socket state into the channel lifecycle, and reconnect with bounded backoff or a circuit breaker plus focused TCP recovery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor guide explicitly routes IRC ownership knowledge to Vignesh.
